items.followUp: What is a scalar quantity? Give one example.

rubric.why: A vector is distinguished by having both magnitude and direction.
rubric.description: Defines a vector using magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a vector has both magnitude and direction.

rubric.why: A valid example shows that the student can identify a vector quantity.
rubric.description: Gives one valid example of a vector quantity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct vector example.

modelAnswer: A vector is a physical quantity that has both magnitude and direction.

items.followUp: Define mass and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Force is described as a push or pull.
rubric.description: Defines force as a push or pull that can change or tend to change an object's state of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying force as a push or pull; the definition may also mention its effect on motion.

rubric.why: The SI unit of force is the newton.
rubric.description: States the SI unit of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the newton (N).

modelAnswer: Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of an object.
The SI unit of force is the newton (N).

items.followUp: Define momentum and write its formula.

rubric.why: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Defines momentum as the product of an object's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that momentum equals mass multiplied by velocity.

rubric.why: These are equivalent forms of the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for kg m/s or an equivalent unit.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity: p = mv.
Its SI unit is kg m/s (or kg m s⁻¹).

items.followUp: State the law of conservation of mass.

rubric.why: The law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed.
rubric.description: States that energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both ideas: energy is not created and is not destroyed.

rubric.why: The law allows energy to change from one form to another while the total remains conserved.
rubric.description: States that energy can be transformed from one form to another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the conversion or transformation of energy between forms.

modelAnswer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
It can only be transformed from one form into another, so the total energy remains constant.

items.followUp: Define one watt in terms of work done and time taken.

rubric.why: The SI unit of power is the watt.
rubric.description: Names the SI unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the watt (W) as the SI unit.

rubric.why: One watt is one joule of work done per second.
rubric.description: Defines one watt as a rate of one joule per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that 1 W = 1 J/s.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second: 1 W = 1 J/s.

items.followUp: State the two conditions for rotational equilibrium.

rubric.why: Zero resultant force is the condition for translational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant force on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the zero-resultant-force condition.

rubric.why: Zero resultant torque is the condition for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant torque (moment) on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the zero-resultant-torque condition.

modelAnswer: The resultant force acting on a body must be zero (ΣF = 0).
The resultant torque acting on the body must be zero (Στ = 0).

items.followUp: Define compressive strain and state whether it has a unit.

rubric.why: Tensile strain compares the increase in length with the original length.
rubric.description: Defines tensile strain as extension divided by original length.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ratio of change in length (extension) to original length.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the defining ratio, and strain is dimensionless.
rubric.description: Gives the formula and states that strain has no unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula together with no unit (dimensionless).

modelAnswer: Tensile strain is the ratio of the increase in length of a body to its original length.
Tensile strain = change in length / original length = ΔL/L.
It has no unit; it is dimensionless.

items.followUp: A mass of 2 kg occupies a volume of 0.002 m³. Calculate its density.

rubric.why: Density must be calculated using mass and volume in SI units; 5 L equals 0.005 m³.
rubric.description: Identifies the given mass and converts the volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using m = 5 kg and V = 0.005 m³.

rubric.why: Density is mass divided by volume, giving 1000 kg/m³ for these values.
rubric.description: Uses the density formula and gives the correct result with SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for ρ = m/V and the answer 1000 kg/m³.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 5 kg; volume, V = 5 L = 0.005 m³.
